I farm in Quzhou County, Hebei, so at the start of the growing season I will stick with the pattern I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That fits my place, my age, and the local climate best. I do not want to spread myself across too many crops, because wheat and maize are what I know how to manage steadily with less risk. I have primary-school education and I make simple, practical choices. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is reliable and easy to manage, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is usually better and it is worth the extra seed cost. I will keep fertilizer at a moderate level, not too low and not too aggressive, because I want stable production and I do not want to waste money. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is familiar, convenient, and suits my normal field work. I will irrigate wheat more times than maize, since wheat needs water at key stages in my area, while summer maize mainly depends on rainfall with only a couple of supplemental irrigations if needed. I will not spray excessively; I will keep pesticide use to the basic number of applications needed to control the common diseases, insects, and weeds. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield, but to get a steady harvest I can manage with confidence.
